title: Qt kit: gate
summary: The Qt Quick kit's gate in both presets, drawn as a labelled fixture of DJDL: Welcome at the default, narrow, short and large window, inline license activation, Finish in your browser (no QR) and the device limit's browser hand-off, the KDE Plasma sheet form, and the integrator's three lines.
compare: The product is the hero: DJDL's icon leads every step, its accent comes from the icon (kits are not service-accented), no Polaris Key mark appears, and the name is said once.

DL1 on a window: two panes from 560px of window, a one-line strip of art below; the end pane is top-aligned; the short landscape window drops the by-line and links instead of scrolling; the large window is one capped card on a flat ground.

polaris-key: the start pane is DJDL's art and the head carries its icon; native: the icon alone on the quiet ground, the head carries none, and the tint, fields and button style are the platform Qt style's, with only spacing and hierarchy applied.
Inline is the default presentation (D-79) for activation and sign-in; the dialog form is the labelled alternative, drawn once in the KDE Breeze form.
No QR on a desktop surface (DL14): the hand-off shows the code, Copy, the countdown and Open browser again with the external-action glyph.
DL6: the device limit on the key path is a neutral callout, and its fix, Replace a device with the external-action glyph, is the one primary; there is no in-app removal on this path.
Button order comes from the platform's DialogButtonBox: primary first on Windows, affirmative before Cancel in the KDE form (Qt only).
One primary per state; the key middle-elides at rest and its end stays visible; weights 400/500/600; hairlines only; the host draws the window chrome and no static accent line sits under it.

Copy is the kit catalog's. The welcome lede ('Sign in or use a license key to continue.') is left out here because it restates the two buttons (DL8); the sibling desktop boards still draw it, which the lead settles.
Board copy: captions are the state name plus at most one clause; the presentation option is named once, in the caption of the activation frame.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots, mockup mode)
designReview.verdict: Good after one fix round: no QR on a desktop surface, every refusal neutral, one primary per frame; the clipped visionOS panel, copy drift between boards and screens, mixed accents on the polaris-key cards and weak polaris focus rings were fixed.

findings.issue: Copy for the same step differed between the boards and these screens (sign-in wording, Back and Cancel on inline steps, offline action, expired code).
findings.resolution: One wording everywhere: the sign-in step reads 'Check the code there matches this one.' with 'Or go to <url>'; inline steps say Back, only sheets say Cancel; the offline action is Try again; the expired code uses the catalog sentence.

findings.issue: The visionOS panel clipped Cancel on sign-in and device limit.
Vertical centring of the TV and desktop columns.
findings.resolution: declined: DL1 top-aligns the panes with the panel's content.
